hints: Resolve perpendicular to the plane to find the normal contact reaction: $R = mg\cos 60^\circ$.
The limiting friction force has magnitude $F = \mu R = 100\mu$.
For the greatest force $P_{\text{max}}$, motion is impending up the slope, so friction acts downwards: $P_{\text{max}} = mg\sin 60^\circ + F$.

For the least force $P_{\text{min}}$, motion is impending down the slope, so friction acts upwards: $P_{\text{min}} = mg\sin 60^\circ - F$. Then set $P_{\text{max}} = 2P_{\text{min}}$ and solve for $\mu$.
walkthrough:
Resolve forces perpendicular to the inclined plane to determine the normal reaction force $R$:
$$R = mg\cos 60^\circ = 20(10)\cos 60^\circ = 200(0.5) = 100\text{ N}$$

Express the limiting friction force in terms of the coefficient of friction $\mu$:
$$F = \mu R = 100\mu$$

Determine the greatest and least values of $P$ maintaining equilibrium:
- For $P_{\text{max}}$, the particle is on the point of sliding upwards, so friction acts down the slope:
$$P_{\text{max}} = mg\sin 60^\circ + F = 200\sin 60^\circ + 100\mu = 100\sqrt{3} + 100\mu$$
- For $P_{\text{min}}$, the particle is on the point of sliding downwards, so friction acts up the slope:
$$P_{\text{min}} = mg\sin 60^\circ - F = 200\sin 60^\circ - 100\mu = 100\sqrt{3} - 100\mu$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Resolve forces perpendicular to the inclined plane:
$$R - mg\cos 60^\circ = 0$$
Substitute $m = 20\text{ kg}$ and $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$R = 20 \times 10 \times \cos 60^\circ = 200 \times 0.5 = 100\text{ N}$$

State the limiting friction formula:
$$F = \mu R$$
Substitute $R = 100\text{ N}$:
$$F = 100\mu$$

Calculate the downhill component of weight:
$$W_{\parallel} = mg\sin 60^\circ = 20 \times 10 \times \sin 60^\circ = 200 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 100\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$$

Form the expressions for the extreme values of $P$ maintaining equilibrium:
1. At maximum force $P_{\text{max}}$, the particle is on the verge of moving up the slope, so friction acts down the slope to oppose upward motion:
$$P_{\text{max}} - W_{\parallel} - F = 0 \implies P_{\text{max}} = 100\sqrt{3} + 100\mu$$
2. At minimum force $P_{\text{min}}$, the particle is on the verge of slipping down the slope, so friction acts up the slope to prevent downward slipping:
$$P_{\text{min}} + F - W_{\parallel} = 0 \implies P_{\text{min}} = 100\sqrt{3} - 100\mu$$

Use the given relation $P_{\text{max}} = 2P_{\text{min}}$:
$$100\sqrt{3} + 100\mu = 2(100\sqrt{3} - 100\mu)$$
Expand the right-hand side:
$$100\sqrt{3} + 100\mu = 200\sqrt{3} - 200\mu$$
Add $200\mu$ to both sides:
$$100\sqrt{3} + 300\mu = 200\sqrt{3}$$
Subtract $100\sqrt{3}$ from both sides:
$$300\mu = 100\sqrt{3}$$
Divide both sides by $300$:
$$\mu = \frac{100\sqrt{3}}{300} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3} \approx 0.57735 \approx 0.577$$
